LanguageData.PSR_MaxSkillLevel_Desc: Skills cannot be raised past this rank. Stat scaling is balanced across the whole range: a maxed skill is slightly stronger than vanilla level 20, regardless of what this is set to.
LanguageData.PSR_MaxCharacterLevel_Desc: The pawn level cap. Tracked separately from skills; with variable point costs this leaves leeway and rewards passion investment.
LanguageData.PSR_PointsPerLevel_Desc: Points granted per character level-up. Spent on skill ranks at the passion-based costs below.
LanguageData.PSR_ScaleMaxExpertise_Desc: On: a pawn's max expertise count grows with character level (interval below), and multiple expertise per skill are allowed. Off: defer to Vanilla Skills Expanded's own expertise limit and overlap setting instead. Either way, expertise still levels with expertise points.
LanguageData.PSR_ExpertiseSlotInterval_Desc: Character levels needed for each additional expertise a pawn may hold. A pawn can hold 1 expertise plus one more per this many levels (e.g. at 50, a level-100 pawn can hold 3). Overrides Vanilla Skills Expanded's single global limit. Multiple expertise on the same skill are allowed.
LanguageData.PSR_ExpertisePointInterval_Desc: Character levels between expertise-point grants. Each point raises one expertise by one level (max level 20). Points are banked as you level up; use dev mode to adjust a pawn's points if needed.
LanguageData.PSR_ExpertiseUnlockLevel_Desc: Minimum skill level a pawn needs before an expertise in that skill can be selected. Overrides Vanilla Skills Expanded's own limit (which stops at 20) so the requirement can scale with the raised skill cap. Set to 0 to leave VSE's own setting in charge.
LanguageData.PSR_TopEndTempering_Desc: Limits how far outcome chances scale at high skill - surgery success, taming, construct success and similar - so they can't spiral toward 100%. Lower values temper harder. Work speeds and yields scale freely and ignore this, as do curve-bounded stats like melee, shooting and dodge.
LanguageData.PSR_QualityCapLevel_Desc: Skill level at which crafting, construction and art quality reaches vanilla's level-20 ceiling (consistent Excellent/Masterwork). Below this the quality curve ramps up to it; above it, quality keeps climbing past vanilla into more frequent Masterwork and, near the cap, Legendary. Set to 20 for vanilla timing. Inspired Creativity's +2 still applies on top, as in vanilla.
LanguageData.PSR_XpConversion_Desc: Skill XP earned from work and combat is multiplied by this before feeding the pawn's level. 1 = every point of skill XP counts.
LanguageData.PSR_XpRequirement_Desc: Multiplies the XP needed for each level-up. 1 = the standard curve (100 x level^1.5).
LanguageData.PSR_StartingXp_Desc: The random skill levels vanilla would have rolled for a new pawn (from age and life experience) are converted into starting character XP instead. World pawns spend the resulting points randomly, weighted toward their backstory skills; your starting colonists keep the points for you to spend. 0 disables starting XP.
LanguageData.PSR_NpcRollStretch_Desc: Vanilla caps a pawn's rolled skills at 20. For generated NPCs this stretches that roll past the cap by this factor (e.g. 1.5 lets a skill vanilla rolled to 20 count as 30), so skilled factions produce meaningfully stronger pawns. The extra is granted as starting XP and spent at normal cost, so a recruited pawn's numbers stay consistent. 1.0 = vanilla cap. Does not affect your starting colonists.
LanguageData.PSR_SkillsLevelNormally_Desc: Off (default): earned skill XP is funnelled entirely into character levels and the skill itself does not rise on its own. On: the XP still funnels to the character level, but also levels the skill the vanilla way on top of it - so skills climb both from use and from spent points.
LanguageData.PSR_SkillDecay_Desc: Off (default): skills never rust. On: skills lose XP over time the vanilla way, but never below their committed floor - the ranks a pawn had at spawn plus any bought with points. Only ranks gained purely from use can decay. (A skill's floor is captured the first time it matters, so on existing saves a pawn's current ranks are protected and only future gains can erode.)
LanguageData.PSR_TechNote: Extra starting XP for generated NPCs based on their faction's tech level, so higher-tech pawns come out better trained. Also adds per-pawn variance so some pawns stand out. Does not affect your own starting colonists. Animal factions use the Neolithic value; factions with no tech level use Industrial.
LanguageData.PSR_TechMult_Desc: Multiplier applied to this tech level's NPC starting XP. 1.0 = the standard roll, higher = more skilled, lower = less.
LanguageData.PSR_ScaleCost: Scale rank cost with skill level
LanguageData.PSR_ScaleCost_Desc: Higher skill ranks cost more points to raise, so progression isn't perfectly linear. The passion cost rises by 1 every few ranks (set by the interval below). Off = every rank of a skill costs the same flat passion price.
LanguageData.PSR_ScaleInterval_Desc: Rank cost goes up by 1 point for every this-many levels of the skill. A passion costing 2 stays 2 through levels 1-9, becomes 3 at level 10, 4 at level 20, and so on.
LanguageData.PSR_PassionCostsNote: Points needed to raise a skill by one rank, based on its passion. Passionate skills are cheaper to train. Every passion in your modlist gets its own row. Costs are not refunded if a passion changes later.
LanguageData.PSR_CurveNote: Level XP curve: 100 x level^1.5 x requirement multiplier. Skills gain no XP directly and never decay; passions and learning-rate modifiers change how fast the pawn levels instead. Current level cap: {0}
